messages.content: I need to sort out Baltimore next. The deinstallation is Tuesday, August 19 and Wednesday, August 20. I have to be at the museum by 9:00 Tuesday, and the last crate should leave around 5:00 Wednesday, though that could slip a little.

Understood. Are you deciding between flying from Atlanta Monday evening or very early Tuesday, and whether to return Wednesday night or stay through Thursday morning? Also, which Baltimore museum location should I use for the ground-time estimate?
Yes, those are the choices. Use the Walters Art Museum on North Charles Street. I do not want to build a plan that only works if every connection and rideshare goes perfectly.

For a 9:00 a.m. report time at the Walters, a Tuesday departure from Atlanta is possible but tight. The first nonstop I see leaves ATL at 6:05 a.m. and reaches BWI at 7:48 a.m. With deplaning and a rideshare from BWI to Mount Vernon, the realistic museum arrival is about 8:40 to 9:05 in ordinary traffic. A checked bag or delay would put the start time at risk.
That is too close. What does Monday evening look like? I can leave the office at 4:30 and go straight to the airport.

Two nonstop options fit. One departs Atlanta at 6:35 p.m. and arrives at BWI at 8:27 p.m.; the other leaves at 8:15 p.m. and arrives at 10:04 p.m. The earlier flight is currently $238 round trip when paired with a Wednesday return, while the later flight is $214. From BWI, allow roughly 30 to 45 minutes by car to the hotel area, plus time to reach the pickup point.
The 6:35 is the sensible one. I should be able to reach ATL by about 5:10. Is that enough time if I only have a carry-on?

It gives you about 85 minutes before departure. That is workable with a carry-on, though traffic from the office remains the main variable. Boarding would likely begin around 6:00 p.m. If leaving work at 4:30 is firm, the 6:35 flight is reasonable; the 8:15 flight is the lower-pressure fallback.
Keep the 6:35 as the outbound for now. Now show me the Wednesday night returns, but account for the crate actually leaving at 5:00 and my needing another twenty or thirty minutes to close out.

If closeout ends around 5:30 p.m., a car from the Walters to BWI would usually take 25 to 45 minutes, with heavier traffic capable of pushing it beyond that. The practical nonstop returns are 7:35 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 9:31 p.m., and 9:10 p.m., arriving at 11:04 p.m. The 7:35 requires leaving the museum around 5:35 and reaching BWI near 6:20; it works, but there is little protection against a late crate or traffic. The 9:10 provides substantially more room.
Is there anything between those? Eleven at night in Atlanta is later than I would like, but I also cannot walk away while the carrier is still signing paperwork.

There is an 8:20 p.m. itinerary connecting in Charlotte, but it does not reach Atlanta until 11:46 p.m., so it is later overall and adds connection risk. Another nonstop leaves at 8:45 p.m. and arrives at 10:39 p.m.; it is priced at $276 round trip with the 6:35 Monday outbound. That is the best middle option I see.
The 8:45 sounds better. Work backward for me. What time would I need to leave the Walters, and do I have time to collect a bag from a hotel first?

For the 8:45 p.m. departure, I would target arrival at BWI by 7:15 p.m. Leaving the museum at 6:15 gives about an hour for the drive under typical evening conditions. Collecting a bag first is feasible if the hotel is close to the Walters: finish at 5:30, walk or ride to the hotel, retrieve the bag by about 5:55, and depart by 6:05. If the crate slips to 5:30 and closeout runs until 6:00, the schedule becomes tighter but still has some margin.
So Monday and Tuesday nights only, checking out Wednesday morning and leaving the carry-on at the hotel. That would avoid paying for Wednesday night just to take an early Thursday flight.

Correct. With the 8:45 p.m. Wednesday return, the assignment needs two hotel nights: check in Monday, August 18, check out Wednesday, August 20, and store the carry-on after checkout. A third night would only be necessary if you choose to protect against a major deinstallation delay or prefer a Thursday morning return.
Before I decide, compare the cost of that plan with staying Wednesday and taking a Thursday morning nonstop. Use a plausible hotel near the museum, not one out by the airport.

The Monday-to-Wednesday flight pairing is $276. A nearby hotel option is Hotel Revival Baltimore, about a 10-minute walk from the Walters, at $219 per night before tax, or approximately $508 total for two nights. That puts the two-night trip near $784 before ground transportation. Pairing the Monday outbound with a Thursday 7:20 a.m. nonstop costs $251, but a third hotel night raises lodging to approximately $762 total, making the combined flight and hotel about $1,013. Staying Wednesday costs roughly $229 more overall despite the slightly cheaper airfare.
And a 7:20 Thursday flight means leaving the hotel around 5:30, correct? That does not buy me much except protection from Wednesday running late.
That is right. For a 7:20 a.m. departure, a 5:25 to 5:35 hotel departure would be appropriate. The third night mainly removes the Wednesday deadline; it does not provide a relaxed Thursday morning.
Then I would rather take the 8:45 Wednesday flight. What happens if the final crate is an hour late?

If the crate leaves at 6:00 and closeout ends around 6:25, retrieving the stored bag and reaching BWI by 7:30 to 7:45 may still be possible, but the margin would be thin. At that point you would need to leave promptly and monitor traffic. If the airline offers same-day changes, the 9:10 nonstop could serve as a backup if seats remain, though any fare difference or change terms would depend on the ticket.

That risk is acceptable for this assignment. I will tell the registrar I need to leave the museum by 6:15 at the latest unless there is an actual emergency. Can the hotel hold one carry-on after checkout?

Hotel Revival indicates that the front desk can store luggage for registered guests on checkout day at no charge, subject to available storage space. I would add the request to the reservation and reconfirm it at check-in, since you will need a quick pickup Wednesday evening.
Good. Do not book yet, because I need the project code tomorrow. Give me the exact itinerary we have settled on and the decision about the hotel nights.

Proposed Baltimore plan, pending the project code: fly nonstop from Atlanta to BWI on Monday, August 18, departing at 6:35 p.m. and arriving at 8:27 p.m. Stay near the Walters for two nights, Monday and Tuesday, with checkout Wednesday morning and one carry-on stored at the hotel. Report to the Walters Art Museum by 9:00 a.m. Tuesday. On Wednesday, plan to complete closeout and leave the museum no later than 6:15 p.m., collect the bag, and depart the hotel area by roughly 6:25. Return nonstop from BWI at 8:45 p.m., arriving in Atlanta at 10:39 p.m. The quoted round-trip airfare is $276. A third hotel night is not included; the Thursday option would cost about $229 more overall and require an early hotel departure. Nothing has been booked.
